blocks.content: Quiz: Why do you use useEffect() with [] to call .focus() instead of calling it directly in the component body?
Tap an option below to answer:
The component body runs before React renders the element
React renders first, then runs effects; the DOM node only exists after render. In other words, ref.current is still null when the component body executes.
React renders first, then runs effects; the DOM node only exists after render. In other words, ref.current is still null when the component body executes.
useEffect() runs faster than code in the component body
Speed is not the reason — timing is. Effects run after the DOM is ready.
Speed is not the reason — timing is. Effects run after the DOM is ready.
.focus() is not a valid method in the component body
.focus() is a valid browser method anywhere. The issue is whether the element exists yet.
.focus() is a valid browser method anywhere. The issue is whether the element exists yet.
React clears all refs before the component body runs
React doesn't clear refs; they persist across renders. The problem is the element is not yet mounted.
React doesn't clear refs; they persist across renders. The problem is the element is not yet mounted.
